**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject manifests with malformed run indices**

When an in-wave manifest has a present but invalid `run.index`, `_by_index` omits it from `claimed`, but the default passed to `claimed.get()` makes the file appear to belong to the requested run anyway. For example, a `runs.json` entry with index 1 pointing to a manifest containing `"run": {"index": false}` and otherwise valid tasks returns exit code 0 and includes its fix cycles, rather than reporting corrupted input. Distinguish legacy manifests with no run identity from manifests that declare an invalid identity, and reject the latter.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject an external symlink before loading runs.json**

When `W1/runs.json` is a symlink to a valid JSON file outside the wave directory, `_runs_of` follows and accepts it because the new `_inside` check is applied only to manifests. The command can therefore exit 0 and compute metrics from external metadata despite the newly documented invariant that files outside the wave directory are never read; validate `runs_file` with the same resolved-path boundary check before `_load`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Require an integer runs-file version**

When `runs.json` contains `"version": true`, Python considers `True == 1`, so this validation accepts the malformed version and the CLI can report success instead of the promised corrupted-input error. Check the version's type explicitly before comparing it to `RUNS_FILE_VERSION`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Compare every manifest's declared run index**

Fresh evidence after the malformed-index fix: when a `runs.json` entry for index 1 names an in-wave file such as `W1/other.json` whose manifest declares `run.index: 2`, `_by_index` never scans that filename, so this default treats the unclaimed path as belonging to index 1. `_fix_cycles` only checks that the declared index is positive, and the CLI exits 0 while attributing the other run's fix cycles to run 1; compare a present `run.index` with the requested index for every selected manifest.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject duplicate run indices before summing manifests**

When `runs.json` contains two records with the same positive index, both pass this validation and both resolve through `by_index` to the same first manifest, regardless of their recorded paths. The command consequently exits 0 and reports two runs while adding that manifest's `fix_cycles` twice; since `state.py init` assigns sequential indices, duplicate indices represent corrupted input and should make the wave report no data.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject dangling runs.json symlinks before falling back**

Fresh evidence after the external-symlink fix: when `W1/runs.json` is a symlink to a missing external target, `exists()` is false, so this fallback accepts `superarmanda/manifest.json` and the CLI exits 0 with metrics. This silently treats a present but corrupted/out-of-wave `runs.json` as the legacy no-runs format, contrary to the new boundary invariant; detect the directory entry itself (for example with `lexists()`/`is_symlink()`) and route it through the runs-file rejection.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject duplicate manifest run identities**

When two `superarmanda/manifest*.json` files declare the same valid `run.index`, `setdefault` silently keeps whichever filename sorts first, and `_manifest_paths` prefers it over the manifest explicitly recorded in `runs.json`. For example, a stale `manifest-aaa.json` for run 1 can override the canonical `manifest.json`, causing the CLI to exit 0 and report the stale file's `fix_cycles`; treat duplicate self-declared indices as corrupted input instead of selecting one arbitrarily.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Validate the manifest version before counting it**

When a selected manifest has a malformed or unsupported `version` but valid `run` and `tasks` fields, this path still counts its fix cycles and the CLI exits 0. For example, changing the fixture's manifest version to `true` produces `fix_cycles: 2` with no problems, even though `state.py` accepts only integer manifest versions 1 and 2 and the new invariant promises corrupted manifests yield code 1. Validate the manifest version before interpreting its run identity or tasks.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject symlinked wave directories before resolving the boundary**

When `<run_dir>/W1` is a symlink to a directory outside the run, resolving `wave_dir` here makes that external directory the trusted boundary. Consequently its `runs.json` and manifests pass every `_inside` check, and `metrics.py` reports their values with exit code 0, bypassing the new guarantee that foreign files are never read. Reject symlinked `W*` entries or anchor each resolved wave directory beneath the resolved run directory before scanning it.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
